hooks.text: Akrotiri is the Pompeii where nobody died.
Archaeologists found a prehistoric city with zero human bodies.
Why did the people of Akrotiri leave their homes?

title: Why Are There No Bodies in Akrotiri? 😳
description: Explore the mystery of Akrotiri, a Bronze Age city buried by ash where the residents managed to escape before disaster struck.

beats.text: Akrotiri is the Pompeii where nobody died.
beats.visual: Panoramic view of the Santorini caldera formed by the volcanic eruption

beats.text: Volcanic ash buried the city, though the exact date remains debated.
beats.visual: Artist's depiction of the Minoan eruption of Santorini in the Bronze Age

beats.text: In 1967, Spyridon Marinatos began excavating the volcanic debris.
beats.visual: Portrait of Greek archaeologist Spyridon Marinatos at an excavation site

beats.text: He found three-story buildings and colorful frescoes.
beats.visual: The Spring Fresco from Akrotiri depicting swallows and red lilies

beats.text: Unlike Pompeii, no human remains were found.
beats.visual: Excavated pathways and empty stone rooms of the West House at Akrotiri

beats.text: Preceding earthquakes likely warned the population to flee.
beats.visual: Large ceramic storage jars known as pithoi standing in the Akrotiri storerooms

beats.text: The people escaped, leaving behind a ghost town.
beats.visual: Modern protective roof canopy over the ruins of Akrotiri archaeological site
